expectations.text: Diagnoses the user's passive-consumption / watch-videos-feels-like-learning pattern explicitly
expectations.evidence: Section 'The diagnosis: you're stuck in the consumption loop' explicitly names 'Consumption without production' — 'Duolingo taps, YouTube videos, watching someone play Chopin — all of that is input. Almost none of it is output.'

expectations.text: Names the 'illusion of comprehension' / recognition-vs-recall distinction (following along is not knowing)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly says 'Following along produces what cognitive scientists call the illusion of comprehension' and distinguishes 'understanding in the moment isn't the same as being able to do it unassisted later.'

expectations.text: Explains why Duolingo / YouTube videos produce felt progress without transferable skill
expectations.evidence: Notes 'Duolingo's phrase drills don't cover conversational recovery, listening under speed, or the ~1500 highest-frequency words' and 'It's gamified in ways that don't produce fluency — it trains tap-matching, not speaking.'

expectations.text: Diagnoses attempting an advanced target (Chopin piece) without prerequisite/foundational skill
expectations.evidence: Point 3: 'Jumping to the shiny thing instead of building the foundation...stage-3 task attempted at stage-1 fluency...The piece requires sub-skills (independent hand coordination, sight-reading basic rhythms, pedaling, dynamic control) you hadn't built yet.'

expectations.text: Includes a concrete daily session structure with time allocations
expectations.evidence: Section 4 provides 'Warm-up (5-10 min)', 'New material (15-25 min)', 'Interleaved mixed practice (10-15 min)', 'Retrieval quiz (2-5 min)'.

expectations.text: Prescribes high active-production to passive-intake ratio (e.g., 3:1 or stated numerically)
expectations.evidence: 'Design the daily session so it's ~70% production, ~15% intake' and 'for every 1 minute consuming, spend 3 minutes producing.'

expectations.text: Includes spaced / distributed review of previously-learned material
expectations.evidence: Section 6 'Catch the drift with spaced review + a weekly mixed quiz' — 'Every day, do a short spaced review of older material (Anki handles this automatically)...Every week, a 15-minute mixed practice / quiz on everything from the past 2-4 weeks.'

expectations.text: Includes retrieval-based practice or self-testing without looking at notes
expectations.evidence: 'review yesterday's material from memory, no notes. Write/speak/play it cold, then check' and 'Retrieval quiz...Answer out loud, then check.'

expectations.text: Names specific resources or tool types (e.g., Anki, tutor/language partner, a specific course)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly names 'iTalki tutor', 'Anki' with Spanish frequency deck, 'Dreaming Spanish' podcast, and 'Language Transfer'.

expectations.text: Warns that the right approach will feel harder/slower than what they were doing before (desirable difficulty)
expectations.evidence: Section 9 'A note on how this will feel' — 'This setup will feel worse than your prior approach for the first 2-3 weeks...That's not a sign it's failing; that's the sign it's working.'

expectations.text: Explicitly recommends focusing on ONE skill rather than multiple simultaneously
expectations.evidence: 'Pick one skill. Not two. Spanish, I'd suggest, since you have unfinished business and a concrete goal.'

expectations.text: Provides a concrete starting template or plan (not just principles) they can act on
expectations.evidence: 'If I were you, this week' section with 7 concrete numbered steps: pick one skill, book forcing function, book weekly iTalki tutor, set up Anki, define minimum viable session, pick time/place, tell one person.

expectations.text: Names at least one explicit accountability/habit mechanism (tutor, partner, streak, public commitment, scheduled forcing function, etc.) directly addressing the fizzle-out pattern
expectations.evidence: Section 2 'Book the forcing function before you start' (non-refundable flights, dated events) and Section 3 'Get a human in the loop' (weekly tutor, study partner). Explicitly ties these to 'Tuesday-in-week-4 you has a reason to sit down.'

expectations.text: Addresses the restart problem specifically — how to rebuild after a lapse or how to prevent the next lapse
expectations.evidence: Section 7 'Define a minimum viable session for bad days' — 'The main reason 3-month plans die isn't one bad day — it's that one bad day turns into a week off, which turns into I've already broken the streak...Prevent this by defining the smallest thing that still counts as a session.'
